english: Grandfather, at dawn I reach the chief's hearth. How shall I speak to him? Speak to him: say 'be hale' to the chief. 'May the gods give you good things.' Now give him the bronze gift. When I leave, what do I say? Say: 'may your homestead flourish.' I will say that and not forget.

Grandfather, I bring the horse from the village, (from) by the sea. Say, what news is there? The village's king died and the people chose a new king. Whom did they choose? They chose the king's grandson, a young man. Is he good? He is strong and wise. May he protect his people. Now did you see the sea? I saw it: a great broad water.
uncertain: mréy h₁épi: 'at the sea' vs 'to the sea'

english: Brother, we two climbed up. The cold is great. The path is narrow and the wind strong. On the ice let us two not slip. I was afraid of the wolves. At night they are on the rocks. I lay fire and the wolves do not come. When did we two reach the peak? We reached the peak at dawn. Now let us two sit.
uncertain: who is on the rocks at night

english: Mother, it is growing dark. Where shall we two lie in the cold night? We two shall lie under that tree. Bring dry wood here and the fire will burn. I am hungry and my feet ache with toil. Then eat meat and drink water from the streams. Weren't you afraid of the night? I was not afraid; the fire protects us. Now be (at ease); I keep watch.

How did your ship break, Wesuklewes? Listen. At sea the wind rose and the thunder roared. The winds broke it and the men sank/fled. Then how did you escape? I seized a plank of wood and swam to land. Now I do not row; I herd sheep. Were you afraid of the thunder? I did not fear; I praise it.

Grandfather, we came back across the great river. My grandson, my heart rejoices. What did you see on the road? I saw ships and rowers and men. Then we crossed the river on a raft. Weren't you afraid? I was not afraid; my grandfather kept guest-friendship (with them). I hear a song of the river; sing it to me.
